svg.title: Fabric Data Architecture Strategy — Domain to Delivery
svg.desc: An eight-node architecture graph. A business and domain boundary node feeds Fabric workload selection. Workload selection feeds OneLake placement, which is the single logical copy of data. From OneLake, three paths branch: cross-cloud shortcuts, the governance and security boundary, and capacity allocation. Governance and capacity both feed into an operate-and-measure node, which feeds back into workload selection to close the loop. A separate warning node, reachable directly from workload selection if OneLake placement is skipped, shows the duplicated-physical-lake anti-pattern.
svg.text: Shortcuts for cross-cloud data — External data (ADLS, S3, GCS, Dataverse) is referenced in place via OneLake shortcuts instead of copied in.Fabric Data Architecture Strategy

Business outcome & domain boundary — The architecture starts by naming an owner, a bounded data product, and the outcome it serves — not a technology choice.Fabric Data Architecture Strategy architecture — Business outcomes and domain boundaries, Fabric workload and OneLake placement, Governance, capacity, and delivery roadmap

text.title: Anti-pattern: duplicated physical lakes — Standing up a separate physical data lake per business group instead of using OneLake workspaces and shortcuts recreates the duplication OneLake removes.

Fabric workload selection — Pick the role-oriented Fabric workload(s) the domain needs — Data Factory, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse, Real-Time Intelligence, Power BI, and others all share the same environment.
Governance & security boundary — Purview-backed governance — domains, sensitivity labels, DLP, row/column security — attaches at the OneLake/workspace boundary, not per workload.
OneLake: the single logical copy — Every workload persists its data into the same tenant-wide OneLake, in open Delta Parquet, so no workload keeps a private copy.
text.tspan: Finance delivers daily positions first, proves governance
and operations, then adds intraday risk on the same owned

svg.text: Capacity allocation & throttling — Capacity is the isolation and billing boundary; it enforces throttling per capacity, not per tenant, when a workload oversubscribes.✓ Capacity and recovery objective
Operate & measure — Monitoring hub and capacity metrics close the loop: observed throttling, lineage, and usage feed back into workload and capacity decisions.✓ Recorded architecture decisions
In Atlas: select a choice → inspect evidence → drill into inputs, processing, outputs, example, controls, and risks.
